text.p: These are leading stories in this morning's Paris newspapers.
LES ECHOS

-- Finance Minister Jean Arthuis reaffirms in an interview the ruling coalition plans to cut budget spending if necessary to keep budget deficit under control and meet Maastricht treaty criteria. He adds state revenue, notably from value-added tax, are in line with expectations.
-- Independent supermarkets group Systeme U considers formal partnership agreement with Leclerc supermarkets, details to be unveiled in a few months.
-- French stock exchanges association Societe des Bourses Francaises posts a 180 million francs profit for 1996.
-- Accor to merge with hotels group Sphere and reshuffle organisation, posts a 1996 profit of 1.06 billion francs.
LA TRIBUNE
-- EU commission expects 1997 public deficits at three percent of GDP in France and in Germany.
-- Prime Minister's office may consider replacing Eramet chairman Yves Rambaud, to impose transfer of nickel mining fields in New Caledonia to independentists.
-- AGF may be interested in bidding for GAN GANP.P, after raising some four billion francs cash in convertible bonds.
-- Daewoo to create refrigerator plant in eastern region of Lorraine, an investment estimated around 427 million francs.
L'AGEFI
-- French state's indebtedness rose by some 70 percent over the last four years, at 3,525 billion francs at end 1996.
LE FIGARO-ECONOMIE

-- Carrefour supermarkets head of supervisory board Daniel Bernard says in an interview supermarkets will be important actors in the adoption of the euro, adds the euro ought not to be introduced while the franc is still in use, but in one shot.
-- L'Oreal expects two-digit growth for 1997.
LIBERATION (Economic section)
-- Generale des Eaux to sell office buildings at La Defense for some 4.2 billion francs.
THE INTERNATIONAL HERALD TRIBUNE
-- EU forecasts Italy will not make the euro by 1999, as three percent deficit limit is not expected to be attained.
